item.observed: Both estimates and bookings use haversine distance × 1.3 and vehicle speed, not road routes.
item.title: Customers and drivers are quoted materially wrong fares for real routes — the server substitutes straight-line distance and a fixed speed for road routing

item.observed: Car drivers see and accept all car rides and rentals; bike drivers also see parcel requests.
item.title: Riders can be assigned an unsuitable vehicle or courier — dispatch matches only vehicle type, not the booked service or vehicle option

item.observed: Signing out calls signOut() without clearing the shared me, bookings and trip query cache.
item.title: Customers' trip history, addresses and account details appear to the next user on a shared device — sign-out leaves globally keyed query data cached

item.observed: Requests older than 30 minutes disappear from driver lists but remain searching and active.
item.title: Customers wait indefinitely for a driver after 30 minutes — dispatch silently stops offering the still-searching booking

item.observed: Search errors show a toast; the map has no pickup or drop selection handler.
item.title: Customers cannot book when address search is unavailable — neither endpoint of the map supports choosing a point or entering coordinates

item.observed: ADMIN_EMAIL is unset; startup seeds no user and new signups default to customer.
item.title: A fresh deployment has no usable super admin to approve drivers or manage fares — startup seeds only fares and no admin email is configured

item.observed: GET /driver/requests exposes matching vehicle bookings from all locations before assignment.
item.title: Approved drivers can see unrelated customers' pickup, phone and parcel details across India — the requests route has no proximity or service-area access check

item.observed: A pricing edit between estimate and confirmation changes the stored fare without reconfirmation.
item.title: Riders can be charged a different fare from the amount they confirmed — booking silently recalculates using the current fare after the estimate

item.observed: A captured payment with a lost verify request remains pending; retry creates a fresh order.
item.title: Customers risk paying twice after a successful Razorpay charge — a failed verification leaves the booking pending and each retry creates a new order

item.observed: The verification catch shows an error but never resets busy, disabling Pay online.
item.title: Customers cannot retry an online payment when verification fails — the checkout callback leaves the payment button permanently busy

item.observed: POST /driver/bookings/{bid}/start has no attempt limit or lockout for a wrong OTP.
item.title: Drivers can bypass a passenger's trip-start safety check by guessing the OTP — the start endpoint allows unlimited attempts

item.observed: A 1-hour rental at ₹100/hour with minimum ₹299 is quoted and charged ₹299.
item.title: Rental customers can be charged more than the advertised hourly rate — the rental formula applies a separate minimum instead of hours × rate

item.observed: Gross revenue and platform earnings include completed online trips with payment_status pending.
item.title: Super admins see unpaid online trips as collected revenue and earnings — the dashboard sums every completed fare without checking payment status

item.observed: Only the customer has a cancel action; an assigned driver cannot cancel a trip.
item.title: Drivers and riders are stranded when an assigned driver cannot serve a trip — the driver has no cancellation or reassignment action

item.observed: A slower earlier search response can replace the suggestions for the latest query.
item.title: Customers can select a location from an old search — address responses are applied without checking which query is current

item.observed: Each uncached search goes directly to Nominatim; typing triggers requests every 450 ms.
item.title: Customers can lose address search and be unable to book — Nominatim calls are not globally rate-limited to its one-request-per-second policy

item.observed: The nearby count includes all online drivers of that vehicle, regardless of location or active trip.
item.title: Riders see unavailable drivers as nearby and may book with no viable pickup — estimates count all online drivers nationwide

item.observed: A signed-out session's previously issued JWT is accepted until its token expiry.
item.title: A revoked user's token can still access account and trip data until it expires — protected requests verify JWT signatures but never check session revocation

item.observed: A signed-in visit to /book/cab submits service=cab and the estimate returns 422.
item.title: Customers opening a shared cab-booking link cannot get a quote — the cab route parameter is passed as an unsupported service

item.observed: Two concurrent booking requests can both pass the active-booking check and insert.
item.title: Customers can end up with two active trips and two dispatched drivers — the active-booking check and insert are not atomic

item.observed: Two simultaneous accepts by one driver can both pass the active-trip check.
item.title: One driver can accept two riders simultaneously, leaving a rider unserved — active-driver checking and assignment are not atomic

item.observed: Suspending a driver changes their role immediately, even during an ongoing trip.
item.title: Suspending an on-trip driver strands the rider in an uncancellable ongoing booking — role removal blocks the driver's completion endpoint

item.observed: An online trip completes while unpaid and the rider can create another booking.
item.title: Drivers and the operator can lose fares on online trips — payment is requested only after completion and unpaid riders can immediately book again

item.observed: A valid checkout signature alone sets payment_status=paid without checking capture status.
item.title: The operator can record an uncaptured Razorpay payment as paid — verification never fetches the payment's captured status and amount

item.observed: Today's earnings and daily booking buckets use UTC dates, not Indian local dates.
item.title: Indian drivers and admins see early-morning trips under the wrong day — daily totals use UTC date boundaries

item.observed: Two ₹32 fares produce ₹52 driver earnings but report ₹13 platform earnings.
item.title: The admin's platform earnings disagree with driver payouts — commission is rounded after summing instead of per trip

item.observed: Missing index: bookings (status, vehicle, created_at descending) for driver requests.
item.title: Drivers' frequently refreshed request lists slow as bookings accumulate — the dispatch index omits the creation-time filter and sort

item.observed: Missing indexes: bookings (service, created_at descending) and (status, service, created_at descending).
item.title: Admins' filtered bookings view slows as trips accumulate — service and combined status/service filters lack indexes supporting their newest-first sort

item.observed: Missing index: drivers (status, applied_at descending) for the driver approval list.
item.title: Admins' driver approval lists slow as applications accumulate — status-filtered applications have no index for their date sort

item.observed: Missing index: drivers (status, online, vehicle_type) for the per-vehicle count.
item.title: Customers' fare estimates slow as the driver fleet grows — each vehicle option counts approved online drivers without a matching vehicle index

item.observed: Missing indexes: bookings (customer_id, status) and (driver_id, status) for active trips.
item.title: Riders' and drivers' repeatedly polled active-trip checks slow as histories accumulate — owner and active-status indexes are missing

item.observed: Missing index: bookings (driver_id, rating) for the driver rating lookup.
item.title: Submitting trip ratings slows as a driver's history grows — the average lookup has no driver-and-rating index

item.observed: Cab, Bike and E-Rickshaw tiles all open service=ride and list every ride vehicle.
item.title: Riders selecting a launch service see unrelated vehicle options — all three ride tiles share one unfiltered ride catalogue

item.observed: A denied location permission or failed location POST is silently ignored while the driver is online.
item.title: Drivers and riders lose live pickup tracking without knowing it — geolocation and location-update errors are discarded

item.observed: Failed requests show a perpetual Overview spinner, empty histories, or no request list.
item.title: Drivers, customers and admins mistake failed data loads for empty or loading screens — list and dashboard queries omit error states

item.observed: An approved applicant's cached customer role is not refreshed while the app remains open.
item.title: Newly approved drivers remain on the customer home and cannot go online until they reload — the profile query never polls or refetches on focus

item.observed: Saving a driver's new name updates users.name but not drivers.name used for future trips.
item.title: Riders keep seeing a driver's old name after a profile edit — booking assignments copy the stale driver application name

item.observed: Admin booking-list and detail responses include each customer's OTP, even when searching.
item.title: Customers' trip-start codes are disclosed to administrators before pickup — admin booking responses do not remove OTPs

item.observed: Two admins can concurrently demote each other after both observe two admins.
item.title: The operator can lose all super-admin access — concurrent role changes each pass the last-admin count before either update

item.observed: The delivered client uses React DOM and the API uses FastAPI/Python, not React Native and Node.js.
item.title: The owner does not receive the requested React Native mobile app and Node.js backend — the implementation is a browser React client with a Python API

item.observed: An online driver can create a matching booking and then accept it as the assigned driver.
item.title: Drivers can create and complete their own trips, inflating earnings and admin revenue — booking creation and driver acceptance do not exclude self-assignment

item.observed: Rating a completed trip updates drivers.rating but not the booking's displayed driver.rating.
item.title: Customers do not see the driver's updated rating after reviewing a trip — the driver card reads the stale booking snapshot

item.observed: Concurrent reviews can write an older calculated average after a newer average.
item.title: Drivers can retain an incorrect average rating after customers rate concurrently — average recomputation and profile updates are not atomic

item.observed: Request cards show only 80% driver earnings, not the customer's fare.
item.title: Drivers cannot see the customer's fare before accepting a request — request cards render only the estimated driver earning

item.observed: When auth configuration is unreachable, the entire app renders blank then sign-in unavailable.
item.title: Visitors cannot view the public landing page during an auth-provider configuration outage — the provider blocks rendering the entire router

item.observed: A save from a stale pricing form overwrites another admin's previously saved fare fields.
item.title: Admins can silently lose each other's pricing changes — the fare editor submits its entire stale snapshot without a version check

item.observed: Stats return customer, approved-driver and aggregate active counts, but no per-role or per-status counts.
item.title: Super admins cannot see user counts by role or booking counts for each status — the stats API and dashboard expose only selected aggregate counts

item.observed: Missing index: users (env, created_at descending) for the admin user list.
item.title: Admins' user-management screen slows as accounts accumulate — the environment-filtered newest-first user query has no matching index

item.observed: Both sign-out controls leave globally keyed me, bookings and trip query data cached.
item.title: Customers' trip history, addresses and account details appear to the next user on a shared device — sign-out leaves globally keyed query data cached

item.observed: Approved or demoted users retain the cached role while the app remains open.
item.title: Newly approved drivers cannot go online and demoted users retain stale navigation until reload — the profile query never polls or refetches on focus

item.observed: Suspension or role change blocks driver endpoints immediately, even during an ongoing trip.
item.title: Suspending or demoting an on-trip driver strands the rider in an uncancellable ongoing booking — role removal blocks trip completion

item.observed: Changing an online driver's role leaves drivers.status=approved and online=true.
item.title: Riders see demoted drivers as available and admins see them online — changing a driver's role leaves the driver profile approved and online

item.observed: Opening a shared trip link signed out leads to landing and sign-in returns to / instead.
item.title: Signed-out riders lose a shared trip link when they sign in — the landing and auth redirects discard the original destination

item.observed: A 100 kg parcel receives a bike quote and can be booked for delivery by bike.
item.title: Courier customers can book a bike for a package it cannot carry — parcel weight never filters or validates vehicle options

item.observed: A 500 kg parcel receives a bike quote and can be booked for delivery by bike.
item.title: Courier customers can book a bike for a package it cannot carry — parcel weight never filters or validates vehicle options
